title: Orthopedic doctor visit
what: A doctor who treats injuries and conditions of the bones, joints, muscles, and ligaments.
why: For injuries, fractures, dislocations, joint or back pain, flat feet, and after bone surgery.
tell_doctor: How and when the injury happened or the pain began

prepare.title: Scans
prepare.text: Bring X-rays, MRI or CT scans on a disc, and their reports.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that makes it easy to uncover the sore joint.

bring: Scans on a disc and their reports
A brace or insoles, if you wear them
Past test results, discharge papers, and reports
A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms
The sore area is examined and felt
Your scans are reviewed, or you are sent for an X-ray
Treatment is prescribed: rest, a brace or cast, exercises, medicines, or surgery
feel: Checking movement in a sore joint may be unpleasant
Tell the doctor where it hurts. They will be more careful
after: Follow the advice on activity and support
Ask when to come back for a check
red_flags: Severe pain after an injury, bone showing, a twisted leg, or you cannot move it: call emergency services
Numbness, or blue or cold fingers or toes under a cast: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: Should I get an X-ray first?
faq.a: If you have recent images, bring them. The doctor will decide if a new one is needed.

faq.q: Are a trauma doctor and an orthopedist different?
faq.a: Usually it is one specialty: an orthopedic doctor treats both injuries and joint conditions.

reminders.text: Orthopedic visit tomorrow. Bring your scans and wear comfortable clothes.
